config.title: Write a custom reduce polyfill

intro.title: Write a custom reduce polyfill
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build your own version of the JavaScript `reduce` method from scratch, called a polyfill. You'll learn how `reduce` works by iterating over an array and accumulating a single result, such as a sum or a combined object. The core concepts involve using a for loop, handling an initial value, and applying a callback function to each element. You'll practice with fundamental JavaScript constructs like functions, arrays, and parameters. By the end, you'll understand how to recreate this essential array method and apply it to solve real-world data aggregation lessons.
intro.usecase: The reduce pattern is fundamental in real-world applications where you need to aggregate data from collections. In e-commerce dashboards, reduce calculates total revenue by summing order amounts. In analytics tools, it processes user interaction data to compute metrics like average session duration. Form validation systems use reduce to check if all required fields are filled by combining boolean checks. This pattern transforms raw data into meaningful insights across countless product features.

objectives: Implement a function that accepts an array, a reducer callback, and an initial value
Initialize an accumulator variable using the provided initial value
Iterate through each element of the array using a loop
Apply the reducer callback to update the accumulator with each element
Return the final accumulator value after processing all elements
Configure the function to handle cases where no initial value is provided
Integrate the custom reduce polyfill into a test script to verify its behavior
